extracted.intended_audience: HHS/CMS/FDA policymakers, regulated health care stakeholders (laboratories, medical device manufacturers, pharmacies), and small business advocacy audiences
extracted.subtask_description: Stakeholder recommendations and critique submitted to HHS (CMS, FDA, OCR) urging revision or rescission of specific regulatory provisions affecting laboratories, medical devices, Medicare coverage/payment rules, pharmacy compounding, food labeling, and health information security. The document catalogs regulatory citations, the challenged requirements, and stakeholder rationales and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory director qualifications (two-year supervisory experience requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement (referenced at 42 CFR § 493.1411(b)(4)(i)(A)) that laboratory directors have two years of experience supervising high-complexity testing and increased educational requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders assert this reduces the number of medical doctors who qualify as laboratory directors, will contribute to laboratory closures, and negatively affect patient diagnosis/care (especially in rural/underserved areas). They recommend CMS revise or eliminate these qualification provisions to avoid worsening workforce shortages and access problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultant Qualifications — removal of nursing degree as qualifying degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule removed the nursing degree as a qualifying degree to operate as a technical consultant documenting competency to run point-of-care (POC) tests in moderately complex laboratories (e.g., EDs and critical care).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders argue MDs and BSN holders should qualify similarly to BS holders in chemical/biological/clinical laboratory sciences as prior regulations allowed. No prior problems were identified with nurses holding these roles; removing the nursing degree reduces available qualified personnel, overburdens labs, delays results, and harms patient care. Recommendation: reinstate or preserve nursing degree as qualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §493.1423(b)(7) — Blood Gas Analysis Testing Personnel Qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule raised educational/qualification standards for blood gas testing, diverging from CLIA preamble language that moderate complexity testing personnel may qualify with a high school diploma or equivalent plus documented training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders recommend rescinding the heightened education requirement because it conflicts with preamble and standard test qualifications, preventing EMTs (who typically have high school education + EMT training/certification) from running blood gases on POC devices during critical transport. They assert trained EMTs should be allowed to run blood gas tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §493.1804(c)(1) — Imposition of Alternative Sanctions on CoW Laboratories
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule allows imposition of alternative (financial) sanctions on Certificate of Waiver (CoW) laboratories for improper proficiency testing referrals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders say proficiency testing is not required for waived testing; these sanctions are unnecessary, unfair, impractical, and will increase compliance focus/costs for waived labs, potentially reducing patient access. Given ~200,000 waived certificates, effective oversight is impractical. Recommendation: rescind these alternative sanctions for CoW labs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §493, Subpart F — CLIA Fees and Fee Allocation Changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to Subpart F implementing CLIA fee updates (including an 18% across-the-board update and allocation of FDA categorization costs to CoW labs) intended to stabilize the CLIA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders argue repeated fee increases have not stabilized funding and instead exacerbate consolidation and workforce shortages, increase lab operating costs (especially CoW labs), and threaten access. Recommendation: rescind Subpart F changes and re-evaluate fee policy; no evidence supports claimed stabilization benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: MLN guidance requiring QW modifier for CLIA-waived tests (MM13858, MM13253, 'New Waived Tests')
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicare Learning Network (MLN) Matters guidance requires Medicare/Medicaid claims for certain CLIA-waived tests to include modifier 'QW' to be recognized as waived tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small medical device stakeholders say this imposes unnecessary paperwork, delays reporting and reimbursement for FDA-approved waived tests, and is duplicative given existing FDA categorization. Recommendation: rescind MLN guidance documents requiring QW modifier for waived tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §405 Subpart B — Medicare Coverage Decisions for Health Care Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory process governing Medicare coverage decisions for medical technology, including requirements and steps for coverage and coding for devices and technologies (including IDE studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders recommend rescinding or streamlining §405 Subpart B because CMS processes duplicate FDA review, causing delays (coding often follows coverage approval). Proposed alternative: combine coding, coverage, and payment assignment (potentially concurrent with FDA approval) to reduce redundancy and speed clinical trial access.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §§412.87 and 412.88 — NTAP FDA timing documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: IPPS final rule requires NTAP applicants to have a complete FDA marketing submission under active review prior to the NTAP application deadline and FDA marketing authorization no later than May 1 of the fiscal year during which the application is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders say these timing requirements are unrealistically rigid, inconsistent with FDA timelines, and have made multiple NTAP applications ineligible, delaying access and harming innovation. Recommendations include rescinding or relaxing timing rules, establishing a semi-annual or quarterly NTAP review cycle (similar to OPPS TPT), and allowing CMS-mid-review engagement with applicants to request clarifications early.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTAP process improvement — mid-review communications and review cycle reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder-suggested process reforms for NTAP: CMS engage with applicants during review for clarifications; adopt semi-annual/quarterly review cycles with sub-regulatory preliminary approvals feeding into annual IPPS rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mid-review communication could reduce deficiencies and speed decisions; quarterly review cycles (like OPPS TPT) would be less administratively burdensome than annual NTAP cycles and could accelerate patient access while preserving transparency via subsequent rulemaking inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §419.66(b)(3) — Transitional Pass-Through (TPT) Payments device eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: TPT eligibility requires the device be an integral part of the service, used for one patient only, contact human tissue, and be surgically implanted/inserted/applied on a wound or lesion; TPT provides additional payments for new devices/drugs/biologics in outpatient settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders recommend rescinding the implant/inserted limitation because it excludes many modern technologies (e.g., clinical diagnostic tests) that are vital to care and innovation. They argue current criteria no longer reflect technology and impede adoption; recommendation to remove technological limitation so more devices (including diagnostics) can qualify for pass-through status.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §419, Subpart I — Prior Authorization for Outpatient Department (OPD) Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory prior authorization requirements for certain hospital OPD services (e.g., cervical fusion procedures) intended to control unnecessary increases in volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders argue CMS failed to show that OPD volume increases were unnecessary (migration from inpatient to outpatient explains growth). Prior authorization imposes administrative burden, delays care, and impairs patient access and innovation. Recommendation: rescind §419 Subpart I prior authorization requirements and related demonstration proposals for ASCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §422.122 — Medicare Advantage prior authorization requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory expectations for prior authorization within Medicare Advantage and managed Medicare/Medicaid products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders request rescission of prior authorization requirements for MA plans and managed products, asserting administrative burden outweighs benefits, processes are often manual with most denials later approved, and requirements delay care and increase costs. Recommendation: terminate prior authorization requirements in MA/managed programs and withdraw proposals expanding them to ASCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §414.202 — Definition of Durable Medical Equipment (DME) conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Current DME definition includes conditions: (1) items classified as DME after Jan 1, 2012 must have expected life of at least 3 years; (2) item must be useful in the absence of illness/injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders recommend removing these two conditions as inconsistent with statute (42 U.S.C. §1395x(n)) and as arbitrary limits that block digital and AI-based technologies from consideration as DME, thereby restricting innovation and patient access.

rubrics_metrics.name: 42 CFR §403.904(c)(8)(ii) and §403.904(f)(1)(iv) — Open Payments device identifier (DI) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to report device identifiers (DIs) for general and research payments under the Open Payments program (Physician Payment Sunshine Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business stakeholders recommend removing DI reporting because it often yields misleading public information, is onerous (multiple DIs per product/system for one payment), can distort the context of transfers of value, and provides little meaningful public insight. Recommendation: revise Open Payments to eliminate DI reporting for general and research payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive Radiation Dose / Inadequate Image Quality eCQM (CT in Adults) — eCQM reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic Clinical Quality Measure (eCQM) measuring excessive radiation dose or inadequate image quality for diagnostic CT in adults across HIQR, HOQR, and MIPS programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders urge rescission of this eCQM because it is burdensome, requires third-party vendor software (radiology data are embedded in DICOM objects that EHRs cannot readily access), creates operational/technical challenges, and its technical specifications may force dose/image compromises that risk misdiagnosis. Recommendation: remove this measure from quality reporting programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Coverage for Emerging Technologies (TCET) and Coverage with Evidence Development (CED)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs intended to provide coverage pathways for novel technologies (TCET limited to no more than 5 technologies/year) and CED for conditional coverage while evidence is developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders request accelerated access post-FDA authorization, expansion of TCET capacity beyond 5 technologies/year, elimination of unnecessary steps for national coverage determination under TCET, and minimizing data collection burdens on patients/providers. They also recommend creating a new accelerated pathway for emerging technologies separate from NCD/CED/LCD processes to align with FDA's expedited device initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR HIPAA Security Rule proposed modifications (45 CFR Parts 160 & 164)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR proposed revising the HIPAA Security Rule to strengthen cybersecurity protections for electronic protected health information (ePHI), with an expectation to consider regulated entities' digital maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders (home health, hospitals, long-term care) argue the proposed rule fails to scale requirements by risk profile/digital maturity as required by public law, creates a burdensome compliance floor irrespective of size/risk, and imposes substantial unfunded costs (HHS estimates billions; providers estimate much higher). Recommendation: revise the proposal to scale by cybersecurity risk/digital maturity or rescind elements that impose disproportionate burdens on small/rural providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA proposed rule — Demonstrable Difficulties for Compounding (DDC Lists) under FFDCA §503A/§503B
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule establishing criteria for DDC Lists (drug products/categories presenting demonstrable difficulties for compounding), with the FDA applying category-based prohibitions to §503A pharmacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders argue §503A refers only to 'drug products' (not categories), so applying §503B-style category prohibitions to §503A exceeds statutory authority. Recommendation: do not finalize any rule that imposes category-based DDC prohibitions on §503A pharmacies; ensure only individual drug products may be placed on the §503A DDC List.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA Guidance for Industry #256 — Bulk drug substances in veterinary compounding
rubrics_metrics.description: GFI 256 imposes restrictions on the use of bulk drug substances in veterinary compounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders say the guidance undermines veterinary clinical judgment and restricts access to compounded animal drugs. Recommendations include rescinding GFI 256 or revising it to better support veterinary practice, recognize the role of compounding in animal health, and streamline the bulk substance nomination process.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA final rule — Nonprescription Drug Products with Additional Conditions for Nonprescription Use (ACNU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates ACNU category allowing OTC sale of certain products if manufacturers implement self-assessment/additional conditions to ensure appropriate self-selection/actual use without provider supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pharmacy stakeholders request multiple revisions: (Revision 1) standardize the ACNU self-assessment process to avoid multiple manufacturer-specific methods and reduce pharmacy operational burden; (Revision 2) involve pharmacy input and standardize POS/system requirements so pharmacy point-of-sale systems can document self-assessments; (Revision 3) allow state-licensed pharmacies/pharmacists to assist patients with assessments (leveraging pharmacist expertise) to prevent patient confusion and potential insurance coverage/displacement issues. Recommendation: FDA revise the rule to standardize processes and incorporate pharmacy engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA proposed Front-of-Package Nutrition Labeling (FOPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule requiring most packaged foods to display a 'Nutrition Info' box on the top third of the front of package showing % Daily Value for sodium, saturated fat, and added sugars with interpretive markers 'High', 'Med', or 'Low'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Food industry stakeholders urge withdrawal or reconsideration, arguing FDA's cost estimates are underestimated (label redesign and potential reformulation costs) and that voluntary front-of-pack schemes already exist and are familiar to consumers. Stakeholders cite significant implementation costs (FDA estimates provided) and contend benefits are unproven relative to the burdens.
